The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1d070a5c4cd8496), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 71. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider any sequence of finite tracial coefficient algebras, twists, and countable group homomorphisms into Isom(X). Let d1 → ∞, l/d1 → ∞, and let Y ∈ D have Fourier support in {r ≥ l}. Then the following statements hold. For (ii), assume that ∥x∥∞, ∥x∥2, ∥Y ∥∞, ∥Y ∥2 remain bounded; its convergence is uniform under these bounds. For (iii), assume only the three norm bounds stated there. (i) For all sufficiently large indices, the vector Vd1 Y has left density on D, for the action ∆, and right density on Dop, both in L2. Their norms are at most C∥Y ∥∞∥Y ∥2. Also ∥Vd1 Y (Vd1 Y )∗∥2,Tr ⊗τ has this bound. (ii) If supp b x ⊂ {r ≤ a}, a/d1 → 0, then ∥Vd1 (xY ) − ∆(x)Vd1 Y ∥2 −→ 0, ∥Vd1 (Y x) − (Vd1 Y )x∥2 −→ 0. The lift in these formulas uses the same d1; the products have support in {r ≥ l − a}. (iii) Suppose Z ∈ L2(D) is another column with Fourier support in {r ≥ l}, and x ∈ D is bounded. Suppose that for every contributing triple h ∈ supp b Y , hk ∈ supp b Z, k ∈ supp b x, one has d∂X(h+ , (hk)+ ) ≤ e−cl′ , c > 0, l′ /d1 −→ ∞. Then (7.11) ⟨Vd1 Z, (Vd1 Y )x⟩ − ⟨Z, Y x⟩ −→ 0. The assertion holds uniformly with ∥x∥∞, ∥Y ∥2, ∥Z∥2 bounded. All assertions remain valid for finite matrix versions and for measurable fields, with the indicated operator bounds uniform and the indicated Hilbert bounds taken in the integrated tracial norms.
